title: Agents Are Systems, Not Models: Rethinking Agentic Evaluation
abstract: arXiv:2610.01618v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agent evaluations increasingly go beyond a single success rate, reporting metrics such as cost, consistency, and robustness. Yet they typically treat the agent itself as fixed. In practice, an agent is a configurable system: users decide what to tell it, how long to let it run, and which model to use, and each of these choices can change how well and how consistently it performs. We study these choices on a new benchmark of four scientific tasks, where a coding agent must find and correctly operate a published specialist model. We investigate five parts of the agent's configuration: task information, reasoning, self-verification, time budget, and backbone model. We find substantial run-to-run variability, with approximately 54% of the outcome variance coming from repeating the same configuration rather than changing it. translated_title: 智能体是系统，而非模型：重新思考智能体评估
translated_abstract: arXiv:2610.01618v1 公告类型：新 摘要：智能体评估已越来越多地超越单一的成功率，开始报告成本、一致性和鲁棒性等指标。然而，这些评估通常将智能体本身视为固定的。在实践中，智能体是一个可配置的系统：用户决定向它提供什么信息、让它运行多长时间以及使用哪个模型，而这些选择中的每一项都可能改变其表现水平和一致性。我们在一个包含四项科学任务的新基准上研究这些选择，在该基准中，一个编程智能体必须找到并正确操作已发表的专门领域模型。我们研究了智能体配置的五个部分：任务信息、推理、自我验证、时间预算和骨干模型。我们发现运行之间存在显著的变异性，约54%的结果方差来自重复相同配置而非更改配置。在不同配置之间，提供给智能体的信息影响最大，超过了时间预算和骨干模型。
tldr: 该论文主张将智能体视为可配置的系统而非固定模型进行评估，通过对任务信息、推理、自我验证、时间预算和骨干模型五项配置的研究，发现约54%的结果方差来自相同配置的重复运行，而提供给智能体的任务信息是影响性能的最大因素。
en_tdlr: The paper argues that agents should be evaluated as configurable systems rather than fixed models, finding that about 54% of outcome variance comes from repeating the same configuration and that the information provided to the agent has the largest effect on performance.
